#Guptaleaks

By: Graham Coetzer | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A treasure trove of leaked emails reveal the extent of state capture by the Gupta family

Unique Selling Point:
amaBhungane and Scorpio have revealed that they are in possession of between 100 000 to 200 000 leaked emails and documents, some of which allegedly implicate the minister of finance in colluding with the Gupta family, as well as a host of other allegations that if true prove just how rotten to the core the South African government has become.

Summary:
The emails show that President Jacob Zuma's friends the Guptas are diverting billionds of rands from Transnet's purchase of locomotives to their offshore accounts. That the Gupta's were able to capture Home Affairs officials, two of which were specifically placed in India by the home affairs minister Malusi Gigaba. The leaks expose the extent to which Matshela Koko from Eskom has been captured by the Guptas.The president's son, Duduzane Zuma has been captured and influences decision making on behalf of the Gupta's, even his father's. The Gupta's R330 million rand mansion in Dubai is often used as a venue for visiting execs from SOE's.

#Guptaleaks
2 June 2017

Voice
From the Nkandla debacle to the Public Protector’s state of capture report, its been a busy few years for the Zuma presidency; and hardly a week seems to go by without some new controversy hitting the headlines. (12.14 Sec)

Link John
The latest scandal involves a trove of emails that have shaken the very foundations of the political establishment. They expose for the first time the full extent of state capture in this country and while complex, this is the gist of what you need to know.

Voice
This week the amaBhunghane Centre for Investigative Journalism together with the Daily Maverick’s newly established investigative division Scorpio revealed they were in possession of about 200 000 leaked emails and documents, many of which support allegations of state capture by the controversial Gupta family. (19 sec)

Sound Up Sam Sole
The Gupta’s were the center of state capture, and now these emails really provide a lot more evidence of what was going on in the background.

Voice
We caught up with amaBhungane’s managing partner Sam Sole in Cape Town. He says the emails reveal just how brazen the Gupta family dealings in South Africa have become. (11 Sec)

Sound Up Sam
This is why the questions around President Jacob Zuma are so crucial, because nobody could operate this way unless they believed they had the protection of the state essentially. The head of state and his ability to control other arms of the state.

Voice
The first revelations to come from the emails now known as the #Guptaleaks allege that
The Guptas received a kickback of about R5.3 billion rand in return for securing a lucrative contract for Chinese Company China South Rail to supply locomotives to Transnet
The president’s son Duduzane Zuma benefits from his close relationship with the Gupta’s and provides a key line of communication for them
The extent to which former Eskom acting chief executive Matshela Koko was captured
The rot has spread from officials in various government departments and state owned enterprises to ministers and finally the president. (39.20 sec)

Sound Up Susan Comrie
John: As you’re going through this information, do you find yourself being surprised, shocked?

Susan: So we had a sense of what was happening, but for me personally it’s far worse than we actually imagined. In terms of the level of access they have, the brazenness, the degree to which it feels like they own state owned companies.

Voice
Susan Comrie is an investigative journalist at amaBhungane. She says the nearly 1 terabyte of data that comprises the Guptaleaks provides an insight into the very heart of the family’s empire. (12.08 sec)

Sound Up Susan
You’re seeing a lot of stories coming out now, but those are effectively where people have been able to go into the trove and search for someone’s name and things pop up. The really difficult work is reconstructing all of the payments and how the companies all link together.

Link John
One of the most startling revelations relates to Transnet’s acquisition of locomotives. Its emerged that a Gupta linked company was paid around R5.3 billion for offering what was effectively, advice.

Sound Up Susan
A couple of years ago Transnet decided to order a massive number of locomotives.

Voice
Under then minister of public enterprises Malusi Gigaba’s tenure, Transnet ordered 1064 locomotives at a cost of R25 billion. The lion’s share of the contract went to a company called China South Rail. (14.10 sec)

Sound Up Susan
Now what’s emerged is that you have a company called Tequesta that’s going to benefit, they are going to take around 21% of everything that flows to China South Rail that will go to this company Tequesta.


Voice
Tequesta Group Ltd is linked to the Gupta’s through Salim Essa who represents a broader network of Gupta interests. The question is why would they earn 21% or nearly R5.3 billion from the contract? (13.17 sec)

Sound Up Susan
Well it turns out from the documents we have, and that we’ve published, we’ve made available for everyone to read, Tequesta all they had to do was to ensure that China South Rail got the contract. Now for that they will take around R10 million on every single R50 million locomotive that Transnet purchases.

Voice
Sole says the deal amounts to a kickback for the Gupta’s in return for securing the contract. (5.13 sec)

Sound Up Sam Sole
Essentially what we uncovered was a kickback agreement to put it bluntly. The scale of that daylight robbery is breathtaking. In terms of the percentage it eclipses the arms deal.

Link John
President Zuma has bounced back from every controversy he’s faced, and while it’s probably to early to say whether this time will be any different, there’s a growing sense that we’ve entered the endgame.

Voice
Political analyst Ralph Mathekga says the Guptaleaks have taken South Africans concerns about who is really in charge of the country to a whole new level. (9.13 sec)

Sound Up Ralph
It is quite a concern when people have to ask in a country as to who is in charge. Is it the president who’s supposed to carry the political mandate or has the mandate shifted, being carried by someone else. Or has that mandate been destabilized. That is quite worrying.

Voice
Save SA’s Sipho Pityana says South Africans over the past few months have shown that they will no longer standby idly while state coffers are looted. (9.07 sec)


Sound Up Sipho
John: We interviewed you some time ago Mr. Pityana and you got quite emotional. So several months down the line are you felling more encouraged?

Sipho: I’m so encouraged by the overwhelming unity across political spectrum by South Africans, even in the face of a president who is trying to play the race card, South Africans saying that you are selling all of us out, black and white, and this is our country and we are not going to allow you.

Voice
While opposition parties boycotted the budget vote in parliament this week, President Zuma said that he welcomed an enquiry into state capture. (8.17 sec)

Sound Up President Jacob Zuma
There should be an enquiry into state capture by the business community.

Link John
President Zuma this week said he’s not opposed to the idea of a judicial commission of enquiry into state capture, but the emails appear to have added a renewed urgency to the matter and even the ANC are saying that they are not prepared to wait that long, they’re insisting on an earlier investigation.

Voice
amaBhunghane say the emails cast more doubt on the nature of President Zuma’s son Duduzane’s relationship with the Guptas’s and the role he plays for them in influencing decision makers. (11 sec)

Sound Up Susan
Duduzane Zuma, I think if you go back and look at his rise through the Gupta ranks, they’ve always said that he had started in one of their companies and genuinely worked his way up. I think if you go back and you look at how his shareholding changed, it’s very clear that as soon as Zuma became president he suddenly started being handed shares in companies, he suddenly started being placed in all these influential positions.

Voice
Comrie says that because of complex corporate structures Zuma doesn’t have much power in the companies he owns shares in. (7.05 sec)

Sound Up Susan
And he effectively becomes, from what we can tell, becomes a really useful asset for them. But an asset none the less that’s there to be used and manipulated.

Voice
David Lewis is the Executive Director of Corruption Watch. He says Duduzane’s ties to the Gupta’s are a clear conflict of interest. (8.02 sec)

Sound Up David
You know I remember many years ago when President Zuma said rhetorically but what’s wrong with my family being in business? Well you know what’s wrong with your family being in the businesses that he is in is that they happen all to be businesses that seriously benefit from and require the compliance and the cooperation of the state. And on all accounts that’s wrong.

Sound Up Sam Sole
In terms of his salary, what we discovered is, at least in terms of director’s fees, he’s the highest paid of all their employees including the Gupta brothers.

Voice
The leaks are also adding more flesh to the bones of the already damning evidence of capture of our state owned enterprises. (7.17 sec)

Sound Up Susan
John: You’ve also described Matshela Koko as being compromised, how so?

Susan: Absolutely. I mean you’ll remember well Matshela Koko being interviewed on Carte Blanche in 2016 where he had the famous line “let’s say I made a mistake”.

Sound Up CB Insert Optimum Coal 1
Matshela Koko: I’m not aware that it’s paid, but in the event that it’s paid, in the event it’s paid it’s not unusual.

Devi: No Mr. Koko we are not moving on from this as quickly as you would like me to move on-

Koko: No, no, no but let’s say, let’s I made a mistake. Let’s say that.

Devi: Not let’s say, you’ve made a mistake.

Koko: Ok I made a mistake, let’s do that.

Voice
In that interview the Eskom executive was being confronted about a prepayment that Eskom had made to Tegeta, a Gupta owned company, which would help them purchase the Optimum Coal Mine. It was the first time questions were raised about Matshela Koko having been possibly captured by the Guptas. (17.07 sec)

Sound Up Susan
What the emails reveal is the way in which he sort of constantly throughout 2015 when they started getting into Eskom, and throughout 2016, right up until the point where he becomes the acting CEO of Eskom, he’s later then suspended, but it shows the degree to which he assists them in numerous ways.

Sound Up Sam
One of the things we uncovered was Matshela Koko sending emails to one of the Gupta Lieutenants, with confidential Eskom information.


Voice
Information that benefitted the Guptas in purchasing Optimum. (5.07 sec)

Link John
The question now is whether these emails will lead to a criminal investigation, but the early signs aren’t particularly good. The Hawks have made it known that they intend quizzing the journalists, about their sources.

Sound Up Susan
If the Hawks do want to come and chat to us, hopefully it would be so that they can find out what investigations they should be doing into the Gupta’s and not to try and investigate where this information has come from.

Voice
Carte Blanche invited all the individuals implicated in the Guptaleaks to on camera interviews, but no one took us up on the offer. Gert van der Merwe, attorney for the Gupta brothers, told Carte Blanche that his clients are overseas and he has been unable to consult with them, but that they support the institution of a judicial enquiry and would cooperate fully with it. Meanwhile only time will tell if the combined pressure from the media, civil society and the public will eventually separate the truth from fiction. (31.01 sec)

Sound Up Sipho Pityana
South Africans need to remember that our political differences and our racial differences will count for nothing when this country is gone to thugs and thieves. And our unity is absolutely important, we have to work together.
